# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

## Headline

Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable — field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB, AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it** the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms (`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels; the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a *minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up (P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification** (no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change, so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`); it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling, hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade / mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7 teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not** change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests; generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`, run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`, `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired; hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex` auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene: round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart, every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD; otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.
- **HUD coupling (assumption):** the shared HUD has no power-up level readout; keep the new readout gym-local to avoid changing shared HUD behaviour.
- **Parity-test flakiness (risk):** booting two Phaser games per case under parallel load is slow; reuse the existing generous timeout pattern and a single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots.
- **Reset-on-run-restart (ambiguity):** the gym must offer a deterministic way to exercise `resetPowerUpLevels` for the reset test; expose a public restart/reset hook (test-only seam) rather than relying on a real GameOver.
- **Determinism (constraint):** all tests drive `tick(dt)`, no wall-clock.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups (parent / `discovered-from`). Ships the model this gym demonstrates.
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wire power-up level curves into `EffectsRegistry` and the shared effect path (predecessor; makes field pickups level up).
- **AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB** — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the hold-full choice.
- **AH-0MUWGD0EN008T3TY** — P4 model: `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` replace `bombCharges` (supersedes the original P4 axis).
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** — Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration tests (the direct structural precedent; mirrors the same shape for weapons).
- **AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA** — Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining core-code duplication (the parity convention this item must respect).
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** — Test: P10 parity across `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (precedent for real-gym parity tests).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD** – Documentation for combat spawning (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, assert, body (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, applies, assert, body, combatscene (+20 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, body, combatscene (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was conducted: the seed context plus the shipped model, the wiring predecessors and the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent were sufficient to draft a clear brief (intake SKILL §4 — skip the interview when seed context suffices; AGENTS.md — do not ask unnecessary questions). Each apparent design choice is recorded below with the evidence that resolved it and the documented assumption taken where evidence was partial.

- **Q (resolved from the work item + precedent): Should this be a new dedicated gym or an extension of `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymPowerUpsUtility`?** — Answer: a **new** `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene. Evidence: the work-item title and description say "Add a gym scene"; the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent (AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J) established a dedicated leveling gym; `GymIndex` auto-discovers `Gym<Name>.ts`. Source: work-item description; `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- **Q (resolved from the work item): What is the parity-test scope?** — Answer: boot the **real** gym and assert the shared power-up level path is identical to `PlayScene`, not another minimal `EquivGymScene`. Evidence: the description explicitly requires game↔gym parity "for the shared power-up level path" and names the duplicate-body guard. Source: work-item description; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): Should the gym include combat threats so P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour is fully observable?** — Answer (assumed, producer may override): threat-free readout gallery as the default, with an optional threat toggle only if the parity tests require observable combat behaviour. Evidence: `GymWeaponLeveling` is threat-free and demonstrates levels via a readout; `GymPowerUpsCombat` already owns the threat-based P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour. Source: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): What demonstrates "level" — a shared HUD readout or a gym-local panel?** — Answer (assumed): gym-local readout over `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`; avoid changing shared HUD behaviour. Evidence: the shared HUD has only a weapon-level readout; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the established gym-local `.gym-panel` pattern. Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): How does the gym exercise level reset?** — Answer (assumed): expose a deterministic public restart/reset hook on the gym scene so the reset test does not depend on a real GameOver sequence. Source: `Player.getPowerUpLevels` / `resetPowerUpLevels` (`src/entities/Player.ts`).
- **Observation:** the automated `find-related` report surfaced only generic matches (enemy gym, difficulty curve, combat-spawning docs); the higher-signal relationships above were found by manual worklog search and file inspection.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-14:** Plan skill executed. Decomposed into 3 children:
  1. AH-0MV7QKEEO006WFI1 — Implement GymPowerUpLeveling gym scene with integration tests (covers parent AC1–AC3)
  2. AH-0MV7QSZMW009OA75 — Game↔gym parity tests for the power-up level path (covers parent AC4)
  3. AH-0MV7QVOAG003U8AA — Document the GymPowerUpLeveling gym and verify the full suite (covers parent AC5–AC6)
- Dependency edges: parity depends on gym, docs depends on gym.
- Effort/risk: Small / Medium, score 6. Recommended 20.17h.
- Six automated review stages passed.
- AC coverage: all 6 parent ACs covered by children (see comment AH-C0MV7T60R9009Z2BR for matcher false-negative analysis).
- Four spurious auto-closed gap children (AH-0MV7SM4IX003WMAB, AH-0MV7SM4VS001GEWJ, AH-0MV7SM57F009S6QL, AH-0MV7SM5IA006OE9S) closed as duplicates.
- Parent stage set to `plan_complete`, status `open`.

# Scripted Gameplay Videos (Multi-Scene Capture)

In a scripted video capture we create a level, play it for x seconds, then capture y seconds, pause the video capture. Create a new level, play it for x seconds, capture y seconds. There should be a fade to black and a fade from black lasting 0.25 seconds between each scene. There are an arbitrary number of scenes.

## Problem statement

The current capture system produces a single continuous video — either one full demo run with tail, or a fixed-length scripted clip. This feature adds **multi-scene** capture: sequence several gameplay segments (levels or gyms), play each for a configured duration, capture each for a configured duration, and stitch them into one video with fade transitions (0.25 s black fade in/out) between scenes.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can define a sequence of scenes and capture each one with play/capture durations and fade transitions, producing a single compiled video showing multiple gameplay segments for demo / showcase / marketing purposes.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants to create showcase videos that demonstrate several distinct gameplay elements (different gyms, boss phases, power-up interactions) in one compiled video, rather than multiple separate recordings.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — single-scene capture orchestrator
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — scripted bot plan + probe helpers
- `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` — run-end signal, tail/cap logic
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — hermetic tests
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documentation
- `src/scenes/gym/` — individual gym scenes (each exercises one mechanic), discovered dynamically via `import.meta.glob`
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — dev gym index (reached from the menu's "Gym Scene Index (dev)" control)
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — URL-selected dev scenarios (`boss-four-hits`, `boss`, `defeat`) with a page-side release handle
- No fade/transition or multi-scene stitching exists in capture tooling.

## Desired change

1. A capture mode that defines a **scene list** (via a config file — see Q1) — each entry specifying the target, play duration (x), and capture duration (y).
2. Between each scene, a **fade-to-black (0.25 s)** then **fade-from-black (0.25 s)** transition is rendered **page-side** and captured by the running recorder.
3. The final output is a **single stitched WebM** containing all scenes with transitions, written to the configured output path.

## Design decisions (producer answers)

- **Q1 — Scene-list specification:** **A (config file).** A JSON config file lists the scenes with their targets and play/capture durations.
- **Q3 — Fade rendering:** **A (page-side canvas overlay).** The fade is drawn over the canvas by the capture (Playwright injection), so the continuously-running `MediaRecorder` captures it and no game-side change is needed. Because one recorder runs across all scenes, scene switching must happen **in-page** (a page reload would end the recorder).
- **Q2 — Scene target:** OPEN — expanded analysis posted in the comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6` (options A gym scene keys / B dev scenarios / C generated game levels / D generic scene key; recommended A). Pending producer choice.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — new flags/mode for scene lists
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (new) — scene-list config parsing, batch orchestration, page-side fade overlay, and single-output stitching
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — new tests for scene parsing, fade timing, and stitch logic
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — documentation
- `src/` — a small dev-gated page-side scene-start hook, if Q2 resolves to A/B/C/D (exact location depends on the Q2 answer)

## Open Questions (need producer review)

**Q2: What does each scene target, and how is it started?** — full analysis in comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6`:

- **A.** Gym scene keys (e.g. `GymPlayer`, `GymScout`, `GymWeapons`, `GymBoss`) — widest showcase variety, least per-scene work; dev-only scenes. *(Recommended)*
- **B.** Dev scenarios (e.g. `boss-four-hits`, `defeat`) — real gameplay but verification-oriented; each new variant is a `src/` change.
- **C.** Generated game levels (shipped `PlayScene`, fresh level per scene) — literal match to the brief; multi-wave, needs a dev hook.
- **D.** Arbitrary registered scene key — maximally flexible; best as the internal mechanism, not a separate feature.

## Appendix: Interview Q&A

- **Q1 (Map, to producer): Scene list specification?** — **ANSWERED:** **A** — JSON config file. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (Map, to producer): Scene target specification?** — **EXPANDED, OPEN.** Options and impacts posted in comment `AH-C0MV0MM81J009GUM6` after producer asked for more detail. Recommended: A (gym scene keys).
- **Q3 (Map, to producer): Fade rendering method?** — **ANSWERED:** **A** — page-side canvas overlay via Playwright. Source: interactive reply.

Raised during intake of AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (field pickups must upgrade temporarily). The producer asked us to *consider creating a second power-up type* to represent consumable temporary grants (P6 Phase Shift charges, P7 Teleport stacks) whose unconsumed grants persist until consumed even after the temporary level window expires.

**discovered-from:AH-0MUX802450085VZZ**

## Goal
Evaluate whether consumable temporary grants should be modelled as a distinct power-up type/category rather than as a level that is temporarily raised. This is an *exploratory* task — no code behaviour change is committed until a design decision is made and accepted.

## Acceptance criteria
- A short design note is recorded on this item comparing (a) the level-based temporary model chosen in AH-0MUX802450085VZZ vs (b) a distinct consumable-grant type.
- Recommendation (with rationale) is recorded and the producing work item is linked.
- If a change is recommended, follow-up implementation work items are created; otherwise the item is closed as 'no change required'.

## Notes
- This item is NOT blocking AH-0MUX802450085VZZ, which proceeds with decision (b): unconsumed grants persist until consumed and are not removed on expiry.
## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — the shipped (a) temporary/permanent split: `tempStacks` / `permanentGrants`, effective vs permanent upgrade levels, consumable-grant persistence on expiry (AH-0MUX802450085VZZ).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — P6 Phase Shift charge / P7 Teleport stack grant-and-consume semantics.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpId` / power-up descriptor shape where any distinct power-up type/category would be introduced.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 — power-up/weapon model the design note must stay consistent with.

# Variety in weapon graphics (AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE) — intake brief

## Headline

Make every projectile in the game visually distinct and juicy: give each of the 11 player weapons and every enemy attack its own code-drawn bullet shape, per-weapon VFX (muzzle flash, trail, impact) and SFX cues (fire + impact) — delivered as an epic with one child work item per weapon.

## Problem statement

Every projectile in AI Hell currently renders as a plain filled circle ("dot"), so a cannon pellet, a laser beam and a boss bullet are visually indistinguishable and firing feels flat. Each weapon's in-flight look should communicate what it does — the laser should be a line/beam, the rocket a missile, the nova an expanding ring — with matching sound and impact feedback that makes the weapon feel unique.

## Users

- **Player** — reads on-screen weapon identity at a glance during dense bullet-hell action; feels the difference between weapons when firing and when shots connect.
- **Developer** — benefits from one shared, parity-safe rendering seam so the game and every gym stay identical (repo gym↔game parity rule).

## Example user stories

- As a player, I want the Wave Laser to render as a visible neon beam (line), not a dot, so I can read its piercing column at a glance.
- As a player, I want each weapon's shots to have a distinct shape, colour, trail and hit effect, so the weapon I'm holding is obvious from what's on screen.
- As a player, I want a clear impact cue (flash + sound) when my shots hit, so hits feel responsive rather than silent.
- As a player facing enemy fire, I want each enemy archetype's projectiles to look like they belong to that enemy (a Scout pellet vs a Tank shell vs a Boss pulse), so I can parse the bullet field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Every player weapon is visually unique in flight.** Each of the 11 catalogue weapons (`cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova, mortar, arc`) has a distinct code-drawn projectile shape and/or per-shot VFX that differs from every other weapon; a doc/roster test asserts catalogue-wide uniqueness. The Wave Laser (and Dual) must render as a line/beam, **not** a dot.
- **Every enemy attack has its own projectile identity.** One child per enemy weapon: Scout/Invader aimed shot, Diver spread burst, Tank radial, Phaser radial, Swarm burst, Raider shot, Boss spread, Boss spiral, Boss pulse, Boss desperation, Capturer tractor beam, and Orbital-Strike falling shell — each with a distinct shape/colour/feel reflecting its archetype and gated by its existing fire behaviour (visuals/feel only; firing logic, speeds, intervals and patterns unchanged).
- **Per-weapon game feel.** Each weapon/attack child adds VFX **and** SFX for both fire and impact (muzzle flash / launch cue, trail where appropriate, impact flash + hit sound), consistent with the code-drawn neon aesthetic and the existing baked-cue audio pipeline (ToneForge `playCue`).
- **Gym↔game parity.** Every gameplay-visual change is applied through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, shared entities/utils) and consumed identically by the relevant gym scene(s) and `PlayScene`; the repo duplicate-body guard and gym-parity assertions must pass unchanged. No behaviour/balance re-tuning (fire rates, beat grid, speeds, damage, ranges stay as-is).
- **Documentation updated.** README, the Game Design Document and any weapon/enemy design docs reflect the new per-weapon visuals and feel; new SFX cues are recorded in the audio cue manifest.
- **Full test suite passes** with the new changes, including updated graphics command-buffer tests and new per-weapon visual/audio tests.

## Constraints

- **Visuals only / no re-balance.** The epic must not change weapon behaviour (fire rates on the 80 BPM beat grid, bullet speed, lifetime/range, damage, patterns, counts). Only the rendered look, per-shot VFX and SFX change. Existing constants and the beat-grid invariant stay intact.
- **Code-drawn graphics.** All bullets remain Phaser `Graphics` primitives (no external sprite/texture assets), per the repo's neon code-drawn aesthetic.
- **Parity rule.** Shared behaviour lives once in `src/scenes/core/` + shared entities/utils; both the game (`PlayScene`) and gyms (`GymWeapons`, `GymFodderEnemies`, `GymBoss`, …) consume the same code. Divergence only with a documented reason in a work item and code comment.
- **Performance.** Bullet counts are high (Rapid 6/beat, Swarm bursts, Boss patterns). Per-shot VFX must stay cheap: small Graphics primitives, short lifetimes, reusing the existing `src/vfx/` patterns (bullet impact flash, split burst, aoe effect) rather than heavyweight effects.
- **Audio pipeline.** New SFX go through the baked ToneForge cue pipeline (`src/audio/effects.ts` + cue manifest), not procedural Web Audio; fire/impact cues for Wave Laser, Ricochet, Cluster and Options player weapons are currently missing and must be baked and added.
- **Ordering for implementation.** A shared bullet-shape rendering seam (used by `PlayerBullet` and `bulletUtils`) is the natural first child, since most weapon children depend on it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep.** Per-weapon polish can balloon into re-tuning unrelated systems. Any behaviour/balance change discovered while adding feel must be filed as a separate work item (link `related-to:AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE`), not absorbed into a weapon child.
- **Test churn in the shared visual seam.** Changing `PlayerBullet._draw` / `createBullet` will ripple through graphics command-buffer assertions and the duplicate-body parity guard; mitigation is a single shared data-driven seam and updating (not weakening) the affected tests.
- **Bot micro-simulation sensitivity.** Open item AH-0MV03PVZI009870X notes bot tests are sensitive to feel tweaks; coordinate if a child changes state exposed to `botSnapshot`.
- **Assumption — visuals only.** No weapon behaviour, fire rate, beat-grid, speed, lifetime, damage, pattern or count changes; only rendering, VFX and SFX. If a child needs the contrary, stop and re-plan.
- **Assumption — no new assets.** All new visuals are code-drawn Phaser `Graphics` primitives; no sprite sheets. New audio goes through the baked ToneForge cue pipeline.

## Existing state

- `PlayerBullet._draw()` (`src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`) renders **every** player bullet as a filled circle; the `bulletShape: 'line'` metadata on Dual and Wave Laser exists but is rendered as a scaled disc (documented in `weapons.ts`).
- All enemy bullets are created through `createBullet` (`src/entities/bulletUtils.ts`) — a filled circle per archetype, differentiated only by colour/size from `enemy-configs.csv`.
- Fire SFX already exist for cannon, spread, dual, rapid, nova, mortar, arc (`playWeaponFireSound` switch); **none** for wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options. No per-weapon impact sounds exist; enemy fire cues exist for scout, tank, phaser, diver, boss, swarm.
- VFX modules exist for bullet-vs-bullet impact, explosion particles, split burst, AOE effect, player death, wormhole spawn — but no per-weapon muzzle/trail/impact effects.
- Weapon HUD/drop **icons** were recently redesigned ("Symbols for weapons do not reflect what the weapon does", AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D) — that item covers pickup icons, this epic covers **in-flight projectiles**; keep the two distinct.

## Desired change

# Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) computes a shared
balance-statistics schema for **bot** runs, but nothing aggregates the **same
statistics from human player games**. Today `npm run record` (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ)
captures raw dev-mode telemetry for a single human session, and
`npm run evaluate -- --human` does a same-seed metric comparison — but neither
produces the shared `BalanceStats` schema, so the bot cannot be validated as a
realistic proxy for a human player.

## Users

- **As a maintainer**, I want to record a human play session in dev mode and get
  the same balance statistics the bot framework produces, so I can compare the
  bot's experience against a real player's and validate that the bot is a
  realistic proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A **single shared pure helper** (consumed by both `npm run record` and
   `npm run evaluate -- --human`) converts a recorded human session's telemetry
   record stream into per-run `BalanceRunStats` (one per `run_header`) plus a
   `BalanceAggregate`, reusing `extractBalanceStats` and
   `aggregateBalanceStats`/`createBalanceAggregator` from the automated-balancing
   framework — no schema duplication (the shared `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`
   is used).
2. The human statistics artifact **reuses the existing `BalanceReport` shape**
   (`kind: 'balance'`) via `buildBalanceReport`, labelled with a `human`
   pseudo-policy so bot and human reports are directly comparable.
3. **Dev mode only.** Collection exists only in the dev tooling
   (`scripts/record-session.mjs` / `scripts/evaluate.mjs`); there is no change to
   production telemetry/consent config and no new production call site. No PII is
   recorded or emitted — the artifact contains only schema fields (numeric stats,
   seeds, archetype/upgrade keys, hashes).
4. When a recording contains **multiple human runs**, every run yields a per-run
   `BalanceRunStats` entry **and** one aggregate across all runs, mirroring the
   bot batch output. Output is deterministic (stable serialisation).
5. Tests cover the pure helper (single run, multiple runs, empty stream, seed
   attribution, determinism) and both tool paths (record emits the artifact,
   evaluate `--human` emits it under `--out`); a test asserts no production
   call site collects via the new path (dev-only enforcement).
6. Documentation updated (`docs/TELEMETRY.md` recording section and/or
   `docs/BALANCING.md` statistics section describe the human flow and artifact);
   full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the dev-mode recording path (`run_header` / `tick` / `event` records) — no new recording mechanism.
- Reuse the shared balance-statistics schema — same code path, not a divergent copy.
- Dev-tooling only: production telemetry/consent unchanged, no PII.
- The dev tools load the TS core via Vite SSR (as `scripts/evaluate.mjs` already does).
- Artifact shape reuses `BalanceReport` (`kind: 'balance'`, `policy: 'human'`).
- Human tickets are sampled (`sampleEveryTicks`); survival-time derivation uses
  tick numbers with the default `dtSeconds` (1/60) — report `ticks`/`dt` config
  fields are derived accordingly.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — `extractBalanceStats(records)` / `aggregateBalanceStats(points)` (pure, clock-free).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — `buildBalanceReport` / `BalanceReport` / `serialiseReport` / `fnv1aHash`.
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — `npm run record`: human session → JSONL via telemetry sink.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` — `parseRecording` splits a recording into per-run ticks/events.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — `--human` does a same-seed metric comparison (not balance stats).
- `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — `parseTelemetryJsonl` for the dev sink's flat record stream.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure helper (in `src/ai/eval/`, exported from the eval index) that
   splits a flat telemetry record stream at `run_header` boundaries and reduces
   each run through `extractBalanceStats`, aggregates via
   `aggregateBalanceStats`, and packages a `BalanceReport` (via
   `buildBalanceReport`) with `policy: 'human'`.
2. Wire `scripts/record-session.mjs` to write a `balance-stats.json` artifact
   next to the recording (or under `--out`) by loading the TS core via Vite SSR.
3. Wire `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` to emit the same `human` `BalanceReport`
   artifact under `--out` (a pure shell over the shared helper).
4. Document the human flow + artifact in `docs/TELEMETRY.md` / `docs/BALANCING.md`.
5. Unit-test the pure helper and both tool paths; assert dev-only enforcement.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — reuse `extractBalanceStats` / `aggregateBalanceStats` (no change expected; source of the schema).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — reuse `buildBalanceReport` / `BalanceReport` (no change expected).
- `src/ai/eval/` (new pure helper, e.g. `humanStats.ts`, exported from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`) — shared human balance-statistics extraction + `BalanceReport` packaging.
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — emit the `human` `BalanceReport` artifact for `--human`.
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — write the human balance artifact next to the recording.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — surface the shared helper's artifact from `--human`.
- `src/ai/eval/humanStats.test.ts` — pure-helper tests (single/multi-run, empty, determinism).
- CLI/tool tests — record + evaluate `--human` wiring and dev-only enforcement.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/BALANCING.md` — document the human flow + artifact.

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — parent epic; defines the shared schema and bot report.
- **Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation** (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ) — `extractBalanceStats` / `aggregateBalanceStats` / `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ) — the recording path (`npm run record`, `parseRecording`).
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — downstream consumer of human balance statistics.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the dev JSONL sink record stream is the canonical human source;
  splitting on `run_header` matches `parseRecording`'s run grouping.
- **Assumption:** report `ticks`/`dt`/`sampleEveryTicks` config fields for a human
  run are derived from the recording (max tick, default dt 1/60) rather than being
  meaningful bot-config values.
- **Risk:** loading the TS core from `scripts/record-session.mjs` adds Vite SSR
  coupling to the record tool — mitigate by keeping the helper pure and the shell thin.
- **Risk — scope creep:** the `--human` same-seed comparison already delivers
  metric-level deltas; this item deliberately does **not** extend that comparison
  to the balance schema (recorded as a separate opportunity, not scope).
- **Risk:** drift between bot and human extraction paths — mitigated by
  single-helper reuse and a cross-path equivalence test.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should human balance-statistics collection be wired in? (A: `npm run record`; B: `npm run evaluate -- --human`; C: both, sharing one pure helper)" — Answer (operator): **C** — both, sharing one pure helper. Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).

(A: reuse `BalanceReport` with a `human` pseudo-policy; B: dedicated `{perRun, aggregate}` artifact; C: both)" — Answer (operator): **A** — reuse the existing versioned `BalanceReport` shape via `buildBalanceReport`, byte-comparable to bot reports. Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q3: "When a recording file contains multiple human runs, what should be produced? (A: per-run + one aggregate; B: aggregate only; C: latest run only)" — Answer (operator): **A** — per-run `BalanceRunStats` for every run plus one `BalanceAggregate` across all runs, mirroring bot batches. Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).

  1. Human balance-statistics test suite (AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7) — task — test-first.

# implement.py finish build step times out at 300 s (npm run build ~5 min due to audio render)

## Headline

The `implement.py finish` build gate aborts work items whose `npm run build`
exceeds the hard-coded 300 s timeout; on this repo the build takes ~5 min
because `build-audio` auto mode always re-renders all 65 baked WAVs. The fix:
make `build-audio` verify committed assets first and only re-render when the
audio inputs have actually changed, so the build is near-instant unless audio
sources moved.

## Problem

`run_build()` in `implement.py` executes `npm run build` with a fixed
`timeout=300`. On this repo `npm run build` runs `build-audio` (in default
`auto` mode), which **unconditionally re-renders every baked ToneForge
asset** whenever the ToneForge CLI is resolvable — measured 3.5–6 min for the
audio stage alone (machine-load dependent), plus `tsc --noEmit` (~7 s) and
vite build. `implement.py finish` therefore routinely aborts with
`Command '['npm', 'run', 'build']' timed out after 300 seconds` even though
the build itself is green, blocking finish for every work item that touches
the build.

The rendered output is **byte-deterministic**: re-rendering matches the
committed assets and checksums (a full build leaves no dirty tree). The only
defect is the wasted re-render and the wrapper timeout.

## Users

- **Implementing agent** running `implement.py finish <id>` — wants the
  automated build gate to pass when the build is genuinely green.
- **Producer/developer** working this repo — wants fast local builds and CI
  that does not re-render unchanged audio.
- **Repo maintainers of the audio pipeline** (future cue/recipe authors) —
  want a change to manifest/recipes/pin to still force a re-render.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py finish <id>` completes its build step without a spurious
  timeout on this repo (a ~5 min render no longer blocks finish).
- A fresh `npm run build` produces a **byte-identical artifact set**
  (committed WAVs + `checksums.json` unchanged) when no audio inputs changed.
- When any audio input (manifest, recipe, pin, seed block) changes,
  `build-audio` re-renders and the assets + checksums update deterministically.
- `--verify` still performs a strict checksum-only verification; explicit
  `--render` still forces a full re-render; auto mode's fast path is
  verifiable and documented.
- Existing audio pipeline tests pass; new tests cover the verify-first fast
  path (unchanged inputs → no render) and the changed-input re-render path.
- All related documentation updated (build-audio header comments, usage text,
  any docs referencing the auto-mode behaviour).
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must stay within the built-in determinism contract: assets are rendered
  twice and compared; re-render must produce identical checksums.
- `build-audio` fast path must fail closed on any checksum drift
  (verify mismatch must still abort the build, as today).
- The fix should be repo-local (in `scripts/build-audio.mjs`), not a change
  to the global `implement.py` skill, unless a complementary safety net is
  wanted later (operator chose the verify-first fast path over the
  configurable-timeout approach).
- Auto mode's current contract — render when ToneForge CLI is available,
  else verify — is superseded by verify-when-unchanged; keep `--render`
  (`npm run build-audio:render`) and `--verify`
  (`npm run build-audio:verify`) as explicit escape hatches.
- Respect the Gym↔game parity rule: audio behaviour is pipeline-level, so no
  gameplay divergence is introduced.

## Existing state

- `package.json`: `build` = `build-audio && tsc --noEmit && vite build && check-bundle`.
- `scripts/build-audio.sh` (wrapper) → `scripts/build-audio.mjs`
  (deterministic WAV pipeline, AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD).
- `build-audio.mjs` modes: `auto` (render if ToneForge resolvable, else
  verify), `render`, `verify`. `verifyAssets()` already implements strict
  checksum verification against `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`
  (`assets`, `seedBlock`, `manifest`), including missing/unexpected/mismatch
  detection and stale-asset removal.
- 65 baked assets under `public/audio/sfx/`, `checksums.json` version 1.
- `implement.py` (global skill at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/`, git-tracked
  in the SorraAgents repo) `run_build()` uses `timeout=300`; test/push steps
  already resolve `timeoutPerCommand` from `.pi/test-config.json`
  (SA-0MTXKIIRV009MJWG).

## Desired change

Extend `build-audio.mjs` auto mode with a **verify-first fast path**:

1. Compute a deterministic fingerprint of the audio inputs — the manifest,
   recipe files, pin, and seed block (the inputs that fully determine
   rendered output).
2. Persist that fingerprint in `checksums.json` (e.g. an `inputs` or
   `fingerprint` field written during render).
3. In auto mode: if the committed `checksums.json` fingerprint matches the
   current on-disk inputs, run `verifyAssets()` only (fast, no render) and
   succeed; otherwise fall through to the existing full render (which
   updates assets + checksums, preserving determinism).
4. `--render` and `--verify` behave exactly as today; auto mode with no
   ToneForge CLI still degrades to verify as today.

This makes `npm run build` near-instant for unchanged audio, keeps drift
detection via `verifyAssets()`, and never approaches the 300 s wrapper
timeout in practice.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Stale/absent fingerprint (rollout risk, medium).** An existing
  `checksums.json` has no fingerprint field. Auto mode must treat a missing
  or unmatchable fingerprint as "inputs may have changed" and fall through
  to render (or explicit `--verify`), never fail the build on the fast path.
- **Fingerprint completeness (medium).** The fingerprint must cover *all*
  inputs that determine output (manifest, recipe files, pin, seed block); a
  missed input would let a change slip through without re-render. Mitigation:
  compute the fingerprint over the resolved input file set used by the
  renderer (same inputs `buildAssets()` reads), and keep the derivation
  unit-tested.
- **Verify-first must stay fail-closed.** Unchanged inputs → verify only;
  any checksum mismatch still aborts the build (existing `verifyAssets`
  behaviour, unchanged).
- **Assumption: audio sources are committed/git-tracked.** The fast path
  assumes the on-disk inputs reflect the working tree; a dirty recipe with
  an unchanged fingerprint is out of scope (declared, not silent).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Parallelising the render and the global
  `implement.py` timeout config are explicitly out of scope for this item;
  record as separate work items if desired (operator chose the fast path
  only).

## Key Files

- `scripts/build-audio.mjs` — auto-mode fast path + input fingerprint logic.
- `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` — hermetic tests for fast path,
  changed-input re-render, and preserved `--verify`/`--render` semantics.
- `scripts/build-audio.d.mts` — type declarations if new exports are added.
- `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — gains the persisted input fingerprint.
- `package.json` — no script change expected (or document if `build-audio`
  default flag changes).

## Related work

- `AH-0MV880FUX003TB9E` — Implement build gate times out on the ~5-minute
  ToneForge audio render (open near-duplicate; closed as duplicate per
  operator decision — its "document the chosen mechanism" AC is folded into
  this item).
- `AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD` — Deterministic WAV build pipeline (builds the
  module being changed; completed).
- `AH-0MUZJDT88002L536` — Worktree builds fail: build-audio cannot resolve
  the sibling ToneForge CLI (completed; resolved ToneForge resolution in
  worktrees, context for auto-mode behaviour).
- `AH-0MUZ5HW310018DQR` — CI: Pages deploy npm ci fails under npm 10 due to
  file: ToneForge optional dependency (completed).
- `AH-0MUTYVA2C000SNPO` — Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene (completed;
  pin-check runs before auto mode).
- `SA-0MTXKIIRV009MJWG` — global implement.py per-repo timeout config
  precedent (referenced in code).
- `SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0` — Local skill extensions for global skills
  (the alternative repo-local extension mechanism; not needed for this
  fix since the change lives in the repo's own build scripts).

### Related work (automated report from /skill:find-related)

- **AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T** – Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme
  and accept headerless CSV seed format (completed).
- **AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW** – GymDiver AC1 (diver x locked during dive) is
  wall-clock flaky under full-suite parallel load (completed; repository
  build/test-timing context).
- **AH-0MUTYV8RJ009MWKJ** – Audio playback contract tests (completed;
  audio output contract relevant to the baked-asset pipeline).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Two open work items describe the same 300 s build-gate timeout with
  overlapping ACs (`AH-0MV87694J009Z34V`, older/high priority/cross-referenced;
  `AH-0MV880FUX003TB9E`, later/medium). How should they be consolidated?"
  — Answer (operator, interactive): "A: Keep this item, close
  `AH-0MV880FUX003TB9E` as duplicate." Recommended option A matched.
- Q2: "Which fix approach? A) verify-only fast path in build-audio when
  committed assets match; B) configurable build timeout in implement.py;
  C) both; D) parallelise the render."
  — Answer (operator, interactive): "A" — verify-only fast path in
  `build-audio`, repo-local, root-cause fix. Recommended option A matched.
  (Option B was noted as an acceptable future safety net, not taken now.)

1. The level/wave banner background is **60 % opaque** (alpha ≈ `0.6`) instead
   of fully opaque, for both the level-start announcement and the
   wave-transition banner.
2. The banner stays visible for **3.5 s** (current 1.5 s + 2 s) for both the
   level-start announcement and the wave-transition banner, then hides
   automatically as before.
3. Both the background alpha and the duration are exported constants (e.g.
   `BANNER_BACKGROUND_ALPHA`, `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS`) so tests can pin

6. The full project test suite passes with the changes (no dead
   constants/parameters left behind).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** the banner exists **only** in `PlayScene` (no gym
  renders it), so no gym-scene change is required.
- **Readability:** the semi-transparent background must keep the white banner
  text legible against gameplay; at 60 % the existing 34 px monospace text with

- The banner must remain **transient** — it still expires on its own (just
  after 3.5 s), per the GDD's "transient transitions" principle
  (AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN).
- Phaser `TextStyle.backgroundColor` takes a CSS colour string; alpha must be
  expressed as `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` (verify it renders in Phaser 4.2.1 — if

## Acceptance-criteria coverage of existing tests

The following existing tests hard-code the old 2 s hide window and must be
updated with this change:
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` `AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN AC1` (`tick(2.0)` →

- `AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV AC6` "level-name banner remains transient" (`tick` at

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — update banner-timing tests; add

- AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV — "Show the level name in the level-start banner"

# Intake brief — Smart Bomb is too powerful

## Problem statement

The Smart Bomb power-up (Defender homage, AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ) is too strong: a hold-full reward makes its screen-wide pulse repeat every **5 seconds** at base level (and up to every 2 s at the cap), and its pulse radius (1200 → 2400 px) already exceeds the whole 960×540 play field from the first pickup. The result is a near-continuous screen clear that trivialises every wave the moment the permanent smart bomb is earned.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the smart bomb to stay a tense "panic button" (rare, high-value wake-up) rather than a passive auto-win.

**User story:** "As a player who earned the permanent smart bomb from the hold-full choice, I want it to pulse rarely (once every ~30 seconds at first, never more often than once per 10 seconds) and to cover only a modest area around my ship, so the game stays challenging instead of auto-playing."

## Desired change

1. **Pulse rate (permanent smart bomb only):** fire every `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` seconds — 30 s on the first grant (level 0), −2 s per further level, floor 10 s. A field pickup (one-shot) still fires exactly once on collection.
2. **Pulse radius (both permanent and runtime-collected):** base = **200 px** (10 × `SHIP_SIZE` = 10 × 20), additive **+2 % of base per level** → `min(400, 200 × (1 + 0.02 × level))`, capped at 400 px (2× base). No longer screen-wide.
3. **Damage unchanged:** stays 1 → 3 HP per pulse (no change).
4. Resolved through the same shared `AoEDescriptor`/`screenPulse` seam so the game and every gym run identical code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A permanent smart bomb pulses on the interval `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` seconds: 30 s at level 0 (first grant), 28 s at level 1, … 10 s at level 10 and beyond; `smartBombInterval()` reflects this schedule.
- The smart bomb pulse radius resolves to `min(400, 200 × (1 + 0.02 × level))` px: 200 px base (10× ship size), additive +2 % of base per level, capped at 400 px. Applies to both permanent pulses and one-shot field pickups.
- Smart bomb damage per pulse is unchanged (1 → 3 HP across levels).
- Behaviour lands in the shared core (`effects.ts` / `powerUpLevels.ts` + the AoE seam) so `PlayScene` and the gym scenes (`GymPowerUpsCombat` and the shared `powerUpLeveling.parity` tests) run identical code — no divergent copies.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular, "screen-wide" descriptions of the pulse must be corrected in `docs/Game Design Document.md` and `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` (§6).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (including updated `powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `effects.test.ts` and `AoeWeapons.test.ts` assertions that pin the old 1200/2400 px and 0.2→0.5/s values).

## Constraints

- The level model in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` currently stores every variable on the `exponential-saturation` curve (`src/utils/curve.ts`; the `UpgradeCurve` union has a single member). The two new schedules — linear-descending interval and linear-additive radius — are **not expressible** by that curve, so a new curve type (e.g. a linear/clamped variant) must be added to `src/utils/curve.ts` and consumed by the smart-bomb specs. Keep the resolver pure, deterministic, monotonic and clamped as today.
- The pulse-frequency axis is stored non-decreasing (`smartBombFrequency`, pulses/s); the desired *interval* schedule is descending, so represent the change as `frequency = 1 / max(10, 30 − 2×level)` (non-decreasing, meets the model's monotonicity contract) or restructure the variable — implementation choice, but `smartBombInterval()` must return the documented schedule.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): the change must be applied once in the shared core and consumed by both sides; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard in `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` enforces this.
- `SHIP_SIZE = 20` (`src/core/constants.ts`) is the ship-size base used by the magnet convention (`magnetRadius`), and 10× of it = **200 px** (operator decision Q1-A).

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.smart_bomb`: `aoeRadius` base 1200/cap 2400 (k=0.3, exponential-saturation), `smartBombDamage` base 1/cap 3, `smartBombFrequency` base 0.2/cap 0.5 (k=0.3).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `isSmartBombPermanent()`, `smartBombFrequency()`, `smartBombInterval()`, `smartBombAoe()`, `updateSmartBomb(dt)`; permanent pulse timer.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_updateSmartBomb(dt)` consumes `smartBombAoe()` and applies it through the shared AoE seam; `CombatScene.onSmartBombPulse`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `SHIP_SIZE = 20`.
- Tests pinning current values: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` (102–107, 136–163), `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (~596–656), `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` (~810–866).

## Key Files

- `src/utils/curve.ts` — new linear/clamped curve type (currently only `exponential-saturation`).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — re-spec the three smart-bomb variables (radius schedule, frequency/interval schedule; damage unchanged) with the new curve.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `smartBombInterval()` / `smartBombAoe()` resolve the new schedules; comments updated.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — only if the seam needs adjustment (expected: none).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — possibly a named constant for the 10× ship-size / 2 % tuning knobs.
- Tests: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Related work

- AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ — Defender smart bomb pulse (the original feature being re-balanced; completed).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — Design level curves for all power-ups (the model this change extends).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention (must be preserved).
- AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4 — Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch (adjacent pickup behaviour; completed).
- AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4 / AH-0MV1BIUGE005BJO8 — classic power-up research epics that introduced the smart bomb (background).

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ** – Defender smart bomb pulse (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4** – Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch (completed)
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `README.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Curve-family extension risk:** adding a linear/clamped curve to `src/utils/curve.ts` touches shared machinery used by all levelled variables — the new curve must stay pure/deterministic and unit-tested so it cannot regress weapon or other power-up curves. Mitigation: new curve type is additive; existing specs keep `exponential-saturation`; parity/equivalence tests guard the seam.
- **Value-inversion risk:** switching the smart-bomb axis meaning (interval vs frequency) could break `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` / hold-full overlay deltas or the monotonicity contract — keep frequency non-decreasing (`1/interval`) and clamp, and pin expected resolved values in `powerUpLevels.test.ts`.
- **Scope creep:** opportunities observed during implementation (e.g. retuning the *Bomb* power-up, smart bomb visual redesign for a smaller radius) must be recorded as linked work items, not absorbed into this item.

## Assumptions

- "lvl1" in the request maps to **level 0** (first collection) in the code's level semantics — i.e. the base schedule is 30 s and the basic radius is 200 px at first pickup.
- Interval applies only to the *permanent* (hold-full) smart bomb; the one-shot field pickup fires once regardless.
- Damage tuning (1 → 3) is out of scope for this change.
- Radius cap of 2× base (400 px) is acceptable (operator decision Q2-A); radius growth is **additive** (+2 % of base per level).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "10× the radius of the ship: what is the base radius?" — Answer (operator): **A — 10 × SHIP_SIZE = 200 px**, matching the magnet/scoop "× ship size" convention (`magnetRadius` uses `shipSize` as the base unit). Source: interactive reply to intake round 1. Research: `src/core/constants.ts` `SHIP_SIZE = 20`; `src/powerups/effects.ts` `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)`.
- Q2: "2 % every lvl: additive or compound, and cap?" — Answer (operator): **A — additive** `base × (1 + 0.02 × level)`, **cap 2× base = 400 px**. Source: interactive reply. Research: current `powerUpLevels.ts` variables are monotonic non-decreasing with infinite level space, so a finite cap is required by the model's clamping contract.
- Q3: "Confirm interval schedule `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` with level 0 = first pickup, and damage unchanged?" — Answer (operator): **Confirmed.** Source: interactive reply. Research: `effects.ts` `updateSmartBomb`/`smartBombInterval` (permanent only); field pickup path is one-shot.
